title: Qualcomm’s lengthy legal battle with Arm nets it $2 (not a typo) in damages
summary: Two dollars today, potentially billions tomorrow.
body: TL;DR A Delaware jury has awarded Qualcomm $2 in damages in its legal fight with Arm. The jury sided with Qualcomm on two counts, and with Arm on five counts. The legal battle will now go to a US federal judge who will resolve several other issues. Qualcomm and Arm have been involved in a series of legal battles over several issues over the last couple of years. Since Qualcomm acquired Nuvia back in 2021, Arm has threatened to cancel Qualcomm’s architecture licensing agreement (ALA), and Qualcomm has filed lawsuits against Arm. According to a Reuters report, the verdict is finally in for Qualcomm’s latest lawsuit against Arm. The Delaware jury has sided with Qualcomm on two counts, awarding it damages amounting to $2. Yes, that’s not a typo.

body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Good Lock users are reporting a problem with text size when reducing the size of widgets and icons. Samsung states that it is searching for ways to solve the problem. The team has also confirmed a bug where different volume levels are displayed on the Quick Settings panel and the volume panel. One of the nice things about Galaxy phones is how customizable they can be. With the Good Lock app, you can modify almost your entire experience, from adding custom styles and animations to notifications to adjusting the layout and spacing of tiles in Quick Settings. However, as with any software, a bug can ruin the experience. Unfortunately, there are two bugs that are currently annoying Good Lock users. The first bug is connected to the Good Lock module known as Home Up. If you’re not familiar with Home Up, it allows you to reposition apps anywhere on the screen, resize widgets, and more. title: Tired of slow Galaxy Watch 9 charging speeds? This DIY air-cooled charging cradle could do the trick
summary: Samsung has ignored the issue so far, so users are taking matters into their own hands.
body: Credit: aloowak / Reddit TL;DR The Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 suffer from heavy thermal throttling during charging, often dropping peak 10W speeds down to a trickle or pausing completely due to heat buildup. A Reddit user designed a 3D-printed charging cradle featuring a 60mm Noctua PC fan that drops 15% to 100% charging times from 2 hours 10 minutes down to 1 hour 15 minutes. Despite widespread user complaints and makeshift fixes, Samsung has not acknowledged the issue, released a patch, or responded to inquiries. Charging woes on the Galaxy Watch 9 and Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 are well-documented at this point, and users have long complained that the new smartwatches aggressively throttle charging speeds due to heat buildup. Users are tired of waiting for Samsung to fix the issue, and several have taken matters into their own hands with makeshift solutions to get fast charging times.
